quarterly_data.signal: Customers and concentration (DART half-year report filed 08-13-2026): the only customer above 10% of revenue is SAMYOUNG PURE CHEMICALS (Hansol's 49%-owned associate in Cheonan, a chemical maker) with KRW 83,732,098 thousand of H1 2026 revenue = 0.1747 (17.47%) of consolidated revenue (H1 2025: KRW 72,618,819 thousand, 0.1683) and 0.2331 of parent revenue; Samyoung Pure Chemicals' own H1 revenue was KRW 157,290M with net income KRW 34,851,758 thousand, and it paid Hansol KRW 23,483M of dividends. Major customers listed for the parent: Samyoung Pure Chemicals, Samsung Display, Hansol Paper (group affiliate, KRW 34,076M of H1 sales), Innos Taiwan and Mirae Nanotech; subsidiary Tapex lists LG Energy Solution, Samsung SDI, Samsung Display, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Murata and SK On among its customers. The filing says Hansol supplies precursors to major domestic and overseas semiconductor makers and offers customised products and joint development to electronic-materials customers; most sales are direct to end users. No order backlog is disclosed.

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity, utilisation and capex (DART half-year report filed 08-13-2026): H1 2026 capacity (175 operating days) - Ulsan fine chemicals 39.2 thousand tonnes; Jeonju plant 106.7 thousand tonnes (fine chemicals 38.5, paper/environment 57.7, electronic and secondary-battery materials 10.5). Production H1: Ulsan 33.0, Jeonju 82.3 thousand tonnes (electronic and battery materials 3.4). UTILISATION: fine chemicals Ulsan 84.2% and Jeonju 92.4%, paper/environment 75.1%, but electronic and secondary-battery materials only 32.7% (1,374 of 4,200 available hours); Tapex electronic-materials tape 68.5%. Capex: consolidated PP&E acquisitions KRW 41,905M in H1 (KRW 42,072M a year earlier); parent construction-in-progress rose to KRW 36,038M from KRW 12,396M; depreciation KRW 30,093,915,977 (vs KRW 25,148,866,398). The board approved a production-facility investment on 2026-02-10 and long-term facility funding on 2026-05-18 (new KDB facility loans drawn 2026-06-04); a KRW 80,000M 3-year bond (3.822%) was issued 2026-03-06 mainly to refinance debt. Inventories KRW 142,414M (vs KRW 123,785M). After the period, on 2026-08-11 the board decided to set up a 100%-owned subsidiary in Taiwan.

quarterly_data.signal: Precursor and R&D pipeline (DART half-year report filed 08-13-2026): the filing says AI services and data-center investment are expanding demand for high-performance, highly integrated chips, and device scaling plus 3D structures add deposition steps per process, raising requirements for high-purity precursors; Hansol supplies silicon, metal and high-k precursors to major domestic and overseas chipmakers. Precursors in commercial production: DIPAS and BDEAS (developed 2012-2015), TSA (2014-2015), CpCo(CO)2 (2016-2018), 3DMAS (2019-2020), and newly ZAC (2019-2025), DIS (2020-2025) and HfCl4 (2021-2025). Other: quantum-dot and OLED materials for displays (OLED protective ink preparing for commercial production), secondary-battery binders, silicon anode (preparing commercial production) and a solid-electrolyte pilot line expanded in December 2025. R&D spend KRW 17,045M = 4.7% of revenue in H1 (4.5% in FY2025). Estimated domestic market shares: latex 44%, sodium hydrosulfite 60%, BPO 70%, PAM 24%.
